- Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The host will send you a chat message to identify which item on the agenda you

MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 2023

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR SCHACHTER at 7:00 p.m. in person and via teleconference pursuant to
Assembly Bill 361.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Schachter, Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Friedman,
  Nicklas

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Dean Flores, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

Director Naughton thanked CHAIR SCHACHTER for serving as Chairperson for the Planning
Commission and presented him with a plaque in recognition of his service.

VICE CHAIR YOO has been appointed as Chair and COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR has been
appointed as Vice Chair of the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Nicklas, Commissioner Friedman, and Commissioner Romanelli introduced
themselves and were welcomed as the newest members of the Planning Commission.

5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, DECEMBER 5, 2022

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF DECEMBER 5,
  2022.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  APPROVE ITEM 7A.

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

B.  2022-2023 BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT, JULY 1, 2022 THROUGH
  JANUARY 31, 2023

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired about overnight parking due to the construction on Silver Spur
Road. Director Naughton stated that Code Compliance does not regulate parking; however, if
there is an issue staff can contact the Sheriff’s Department.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Director Naughton stated that the
Code Compliance report is provided for informational purposes; code compliance cases are rarely
brought to the Planning Commission unless any entitlement(s) is required for the case to be

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 6, 2023
  1
 resolved.

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM 7B

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220388; ADDRESS: 3571 Lariat Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Brad Spencer and Connie Spencer; A request for a
  Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220389) for the demolition of an existing
  single-family residence and the construction of a new 5,814 square-foot two-story single-
  family residence with an attached 976 square-foot three-car garage, basement, new pool,
  sports court, outdoor patio areas, a balcony at the front of the home, and putting green at
  the rear of the property.

Associate Planner Flores presented Planning Application No. PA-220388 summarizing the staff
report. He noted the following corrections to the staff report:

  •  Pages 1, 3, and 6: Error - 5,814 sq. ft. living area; Correction - 5,964 sq. ft. living area
  •  Pages 1 and 3: Sports court no longer part of the project

Associate Planner Flores stated noted that a condition of approval has been included to ensure
that all the proposed hardscape and landscape will not obstruct any access in the ten-foot city-
owned utility easement.

The proposed project was reviewed in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act
(Public Resources Code § 21000 et seq.: “CEQA”), and is categorically exempt under Class 3,
Section 15303(a) - New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures.

Associate Planner Flores stated that one comment was received by a resident earlier today and
copies were provided to the Planning Commission via a separate memo. The resident provided
background on the existing sewer main and is recommending that the Planning Commission
consider additional verbiage to the condition of approval that no trees are planted or structures
erected along the ten-foot wide sewer easement.

Associate Planner Flores stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-220388, approving a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-220389) for the
demolition of an existing single-family residence and the construction of a new 5,964 square foot
two-story single-family residence with an attached 976 square foot garage, basement, new pool,
outdoor patio areas, a balcony at the front of the home, and putting green at the rear of the
property.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if notice is provided to the easement holder-JCC Homes.
Director Naughton stated that staff did not have contact information for the private easement
holder; however, staff did contact the County of Los Angeles and received no response. The
property owner is aware of both easements, and it is also written in the property’s title report and
deed.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked about the City’s response to the correspondence that was
received by staff earlier in the day. Associate Planner Flores stated that the Planning Commission
may consider the additional condition of approval proposed by the resident.

In response to a question by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR, Director Naughton stated that staff thinks
that the condition of approval as provided in the staff report is sufficient. The language in the
condition states that if the property owner causes damage to the sewer line, then it is their
responsibility to pay for the repair to the line.

Miles Pritzkat, Pritzkat & Johnson Architects, Project Architect, stated that he supports staff’s
findings. In regard to the easement, he and the applicant’s would like to make sure that they
adhere to the City’s requirements and can agree to the existing conditions of approval and any
other conditions.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked for clarification on the applicant’s request in terms of the
easement. Mr. Prizkat stated that the applicant would like the ability to do light landscaping; no
large trees where the roots can damage the sewer line. They would like to make sure that the
City and County would be okay with the applicant’s proposal.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 6, 2023
  2
 Director Naughton stated that staff has added an expanded condition to protect the access to the
city-owned easement due to the existing sewer line that runs along the ten-foot-wide easement.
The correspondence from the resident that was received today requests that the condition of
approval be expanded to state that no trees or structures can be planted in the easement.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked about the condition of the easement. Director Naughton
stated that there have been issues with other properties in the vicinity causing access issues to
the pump station that is connected to this line, caused by fencing, corral, and structures built
without permits.

Lyneigh Palacios, Resident on Palos Verdes Drive North, stated that the plans and the design of
the home are beautiful; however, she expressed concerns with maintenance issues with the
sewer main. She has attempted to find out who maintains the sewer main; she has contacted the
City who has directed her to the county, and the County has directed her back to the City. Ms.
Palacios stated that she is trying to be proactive and believes that the property owners should
know of the existing issues. She also clarified that her issues are with the City and not with this
project.

Connie Spencer, Property Owner, stated that they have no intention of doing anything within the
ten-foot city-owned easement or the additional twenty-five-foot defunct Palos Verdes Properties
easement. If anything, it would be low shrubs or pathways. Ms. Spencer stated that she has
spoken to the easement holder, JCC Homes, and they have no interest in the twenty-five foot
easement.

COMMISSIONER OLSON asked what the County will do if there is an obstruction to maintaining
a sewer. Director Naughton stated that she will need to speak with the Public Works Director and
Maintenance Superintendent for an answer but in past instances, the County has taken care of
the issue or has required action by the City or the property owner due to access issues.

Director Naughton stated that the application will be required to go through a water efficiency in
landscaping review; at that time staff can share the landscaping plans with the sanitation district
for review to ensure that anything planted in the easement area will not cause damage to the
sewer line.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER stated that the property owners cannot interfere with the use by
the easement holder and the owners are on notice that they cannot plant trees that may disrupt
or cause damage to the sewer line.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER provided history for the new commissioners and stated that the
project seems to comply with the code requirements; however, the typical issue is with
neighborhood compatibility and the size homes.

A brief discussion ensued.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220388 PURSUANT TO STAFF’S
  RECOMMENDATIONS.

COMMISSIONER OLSON stated that there is currently a drainage problem from the existing site
that is causing problems to the bridle trail. He recommended that a drainage plan be added as a
condition of approval.

COMMISSIONER OLSON made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220388 PURSUANT TO STAFF’S
  RECOMMENDATIONS WITH AN ADDITIONAL CONDITION OF APPROVAL THAT THE
  APPLICANT’S PROVIDE A DRAINAGE PLAN.

AYES: Yoo, Medawar, Olson, Romanelli, Friedman, Nicklas, Schachter
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application PA-
220388, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination at 3571 Lariat Lane. There is a 20-day
appeal period whereby any member of the public or the City Council by its own motion may appeal
this decision.

 9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386; LOCATION: 39 Empty Saddle Road;
  APPLICANT: Michael Hasegawa (on behalf of Verizon Wireless); A request for a
  Conditional Use Permit (CUP-220387) for a new stealth telecommunication facility
  featuring a 64’-high monoeucalyptus structure located toward the rear of the property
  including 17 antennas (8 panel antennas, 4 CBRS antennas, 4 C-Band antennas, and 1
  microwave antenna) and 16 wireless radios on 4 arrays, a 342 square-foot lease area that
  features 3 equipment cabinets, 1 generator and will be fully enclosed with an 8’-high CMU

Associate Planner Flores stated that the applicant has requested that this item be continued to

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-220386 TO THE MARCH 6, 2023

10.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

A.  COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  •  Environmental Advisory Committee (2022: Olson/Low)
  •  Equestrian Committee (2022: Schachter)
  •  Traffic and Safety Committee (2022: Medawar)

 The Planning Commission agreed to the following committee assignments for 2023:

  •  Environmental Advisory Committee – Commissioner Schachter and Commissioner
  Nicklas
  •  Equestrian Committee – Vice Chair Medawar
  •  Traffic and Safety Committee – Commissioner Romanelli

B.  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE 2023

Commissioner Olson asked about the meeting scheduled on July 3, 2023 due to the
Independence Day Holiday. Director Naughton stated that staff will poll the Planning Commission
as the date gets closer and if there is no quorum, then a special meeting can be held at a later
date.

C.  PLANNING COMMISSION ATTENDANCE AT CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS - 2023
  SCHEDULE

CHAIR YOO noted that Planning Commissioner’s may switch dates to attend City Council
meetings if there is a scheduling conflict.

11.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 230037; LOCATION: CITYWIDE; COMPREHENSIVE
  ZONING CODE UPDATE TO IMPLEMENT THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES GENERAL
  PLAN (Oral presentation)

Director Naughton provided background on the first action taken in implementing the City’s
General Plan, including the adoption of the Public Benefit Density Bonus in October 2022. Most
recently in January 2023, the Housing Element and Safety Element were amended and re-
adopted to make the City eligible for Cal OES Funding.

Director Naughton provided an overview of the changes to Title 17, which will implement the
General Plan. One of the main priorities that will be brought to the Planning Commission are
changes to the Commercial General District. For the next Planning Commission meeting in March,

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, FEBRUARY 6, 2023
  4
 the initial discussion will be on form-based, Euclidian, and/or a hybrid approach to the zoning
code and discussion on changes to the Commercial District.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR asked if this would apply to new construction and/or existing
construction. Director Naughton stated that once adopted, this would apply to all properties in the
Commercial District.

12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JANUARY 24, 2023

B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS - DECEMBER 13, 2022

VICE CHAIR MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER OLSON to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEM NO. 11A AND 11B

There being no objection, CHAIR YOO so ordered.

13.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:01 p.m.

The next Planning Commission meeting will be held on Monday, March 6, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst  Victor Yoo, Chair
